result.title: MIPS: Mitigating Mode Collapse in Reinforcement Learning for Large Outcome Spaces
result.summary: Expected-reward maximization in reinforcement learning concentrates probability mass on a few outcomes, even in tasks that require many distinct, high-quality solutions, a failure known as mode collapse. Inverse Probability Scaling (IPS) counters this in group-based policy gradients such as GRPO by dividing each reward by the outcome's probability, estimated from its frequency within the sampled group. When the outcome space is large relative to the group, outcomes rarely repeat and these estimates become uninformative. Since an outcome can be constructed along many trajectories, its probability is a sum over all of them, and computing it directly is intractable. We propose Marginal IPS (MIPS), which performs marginal evaluation by combining the sampled trajectory with a learned model of the trajectories that lead to each outcome. On Hypergrids, where the exact sampling distribution is computable, MIPS stays near the reward-distribution target as the outcome space grows relative to the rollout group, while frequency-based IPS degrades. In molecular synthesis and phylogenetic inference, MIPS sustains diverse, high-quality sampling where GRPO and frequency-based IPS collapse, showing that MIPS serves as a reliable solution to mode collapse in RL.

AI.brief_summary: 针对大规模结果空间中 GRPO 类组内策略梯度的模式坍缩，提出 Marginal IPS：用采样轨迹与学习到的「通向某结果的轨迹模型」联合对结果概率做边缘估计，替代组内频率估计，在 Hypergrids、分子合成与系统发育推断上维持多样且高质量的采样。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不涉及视觉或 latent 推理，但其「对通向同一结果的多条轨迹做边缘化以估计贡献」的思路，可能可供核查 VLM 推理 RL 训练中推理轨迹多样性退化与 latent 路径贡献分配的问题。
